# AGENTS.md

Moneo is a Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript personal-finance app using Supabase/Postgres, Drizzle, Vercel Workflow, Vitest/Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK via OpenRouter.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Dev: `npm run dev`
- Unit: `npm test`
- Lint: `npm run lint`
- Build: `npm run build`
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e`

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router UI, route handlers, server actions
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — model/provider behavior
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows

## Rules
- Find the simplest cleanest way of doing something 
- Keep changes scoped; follow nearby patterns and prefer existing utilities/dependencies.
- Validate user/external input; Zod is the established pattern.
- Financial truth comes from application code/data, not AI guesses. Keep money in integer minor units/`bigint` and currencies explicit.
- Preserve source records, correction/history, and undo semantics when changing financial data flows.
- For schema changes, add a new ordered migration and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Do not rewrite applied migrations.
- Supabase CLI isn't linked: run it via `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`), e.g. `npx supabase migration repair --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL" --status reverted <versions>`.
- for each thing break it down and for each thing make a commit directly if a big task make multiple commits

## Validation

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test` and `npm run lint`; add `npm run build` for app/config/build changes and Playwright for changed user flows. Gated E2E requires configured Supabase/auth; see `e2e/README.md`.

Signed-in E2E uses one persistent QA user (login in the git-ignored `.env` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`E2E_USER_PASSWORD`). With the app on localhost:3000:

- `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs` signs it in and writes `e2e/.auth.json` (creates the user on first run).
- `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs --reset` empties its workspace; do this before a full suite run. Never delete the user.

## Context
 
 
Read only what the task needs: `.env.example` for environment names, and `e2e/README.md` for browser-test setup.


# This is NOT the Next.js you know

This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.

This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.
- [lib workflow tests need OPENAI key](lib-workflow-tests-need-openai-key.md) — 14 lib/ tests fail on main without OPENAI_API_KEY

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

content.text:
<system-reminder>
Codebase and user instructions are shown below. Be sure to adhere to these instructions. IMPORTANT: These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior and you MUST follow them exactly as written.

Contents of C:\codebases\Moneo\AGENTS.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):

# AGENTS.md

Moneo is a Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript personal-finance app using Supabase/Postgres, Drizzle, Vercel Workflow, Vitest/Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK via OpenRouter.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Dev: `npm run dev`
- Unit: `npm test`
- Lint: `npm run lint`
- Build: `npm run build`
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e`

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router UI, route handlers, server actions
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — model/provider behavior
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows

## Rules
- Find the simplest cleanest way of doing something 
- Keep changes scoped; follow nearby patterns and prefer existing utilities/dependencies.
- Validate user/external input; Zod is the established pattern.
- Financial truth comes from application code/data, not AI guesses. Keep money in integer minor units/`bigint` and currencies explicit.
- Preserve source records, correction/history, and undo semantics when changing financial data flows.
- For schema changes, add a new ordered migration and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Do not rewrite applied migrations.
- Supabase CLI isn't linked: run it via `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`), e.g. `npx supabase migration repair --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL" --status reverted <versions>`.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

'@

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.text:
I've gone through the current Overview (`app/page.tsx`, `home-sections.tsx`, the insights panel, the agent briefing and the wealth net-worth series). Below is how each part of the mockup compares with what we have now. Most of the data already exists; the work is mainly layout, plus a few small additions to the finance code.

## Section by section

| Mockup section | What we have now | What it takes |
|---|---|---|
| **Header** (date, "Overview", Month/Quarter/Year, Edit layout) | Date, title, Edit layout, and an **Import statement** button | Drop Quarter and Year; Month is implied, so no toggle is needed. Move Import into the Accounts card, as in the mockup. |
| **Net worth** with line chart and "+€1,920 this month · +2.3%" | Hero figure, the "traced" chip and the Cash/Assets/Debts strip | Add a 12-month line chart. `netWorthSeries` in `app/money/wealth/net-worth.ts` already builds month-end points for the Wealth page, so I'd reuse it. The month-over-month change comes from the last two points. Remove the "Recorded net worth by currency" dropdown from Home. |
| **October cash flow** (right side) | A "This month" card showing spent, upcoming and cash available | Rebuild it as **In / Out / split bar / Left this month**, plus the forecaster callout, which already exists. **Missing:** income. `loadHomeSpending` only adds up outflows, so it needs an `incomeMinor` total, with transfers excluded just as they are for spending. |
| **Weekly briefing** | Two separate things: the AI **AgentBriefing** banner (free text) and the **Important insights** list (deterministic, with dismiss) | Merge them into one card. See the next section. |
| **Coming up** | An "Upcoming payments" list with plain ISO dates | Restyle it with date tiles (NOV / 01), name, a subtitle line, the amount, and "€total · N days" in the header. The data is unchanged. The orange "Price up €2.00" label can come later, from recurring-series amount changes. |
| **Cash flow · 6 months** (replaces Spending) | A spending-only bar chart plus top category and merchant lists | Grouped **In vs Out** bars. Clicking **In** or **Out** in the legend shows only that series. Clicking a month opens that month's transactions. This needs the same monthly income total as above. **Remove** the top category and merchant lists from Home; they're still available under Plan → Spending and Transactions. |
| **Budgets** | Not on Home. Budget progress is computed only inside the insights loader | Add a new widget using the existing `budgetProgress` for spent/limit, the "€X left for N days" or "€X over" line, and the rollover note. **Manage** links to `/plan/spending`. |
| **Accounts** | A big card with an inline add-account form and an "Update balance" form on each row | Compact rows: an initial avatar, a BANK/MANUAL badge, "synced 2 min ago" and the balance. Header buttons: **Import file** and **Connect bank**. Move the add and edit forms to `/money/accounts`. |
| **Agent team** | Only the banner, showing the last run and a count of proposals to review | A grid with one tile per agent showing its last result, plus a **Review N proposals** button. I still need to check how much per-agent detail `agent_runs` records. |
| **History strip** (recent changes with Undo) | Undo exists for each feature (imports, balances, agent approvals) and there's `/ai/activity` | This needs one feed that merges the latest changes that can be undone. It's the most new plumbing in the list, so I'd leave it for a second pass. |

## What I'd remove from Home
These would stop being shown by default. They'd still be available in **Edit layout**, because saved layouts store these widget keys and we shouldn't break them:
- Recent transactions
- Goals
- Available funds by account
- Important insights (merged into the briefing)
- The AgentBriefing banner (replaced by the Agent team card)

## How the weekly briefing would work
Following the rule that financial truth comes from code, not AI:
1. **The findings are deterministic.** They come from the existing `buildInsights` (spending changes, budget overruns, shortfalls, recurring price changes). Each one already has a type, a link and an evidence key.
2. **Each row** shows a type label (SPENDING / PRICE CHANGE / SHORTFALL, with shortfall in orange), the sentence, an **evidence chip** ("E1 · 6 transactions") linking to the filtered transactions, and **Dismiss**, which uses the existing `dismissInsight`.
3. **Header actions:** **Mute type** uses the existing `muted_insight_types` setting. **Dismiss all** is a small new action that dismisses every visible finding.
4. **AI wording is optional.** The insight-writer agent could rephrase the findings into nicer sentences, but the numbers would always come from the findings. For a first version I'd ship deterministic text only.
5. **"Preview move"** (e.g. move €300 from savings to cover a shortfall) would be a later addition.

## Questions before I start
1. **Briefing timing:** should it be truly **weekly** (a snapshot taken once a week, which needs a stored briefing and a scheduled job), or **live** (computed when the page loads, as insights are now)? I recommend live, labelled "Briefing", with the date of the newest finding.
2. **Removed widgets:** keep them as optional choices in Edit layout (my recommendation), or delete them completely?
3. **Scope of this pass:** I suggest net worth chart → cash-flow card → 6-month cash-flow chart → Coming up → Budgets → Briefing → Accounts restyle, with one commit for each. Agent team and History would follow in a second pass. Does that order work for you?
4. **Multi-currency net worth chart:** the Wealth page series doesn't convert currencies; it just plots amounts already in the display currency. Should the Home chart convert with dated FX rates (more work, but correct), or only plot display-currency amounts and show a "partial" tag when other currencies are left out?

Once you answer these, I'll start on the first piece.

content.thinking:
Since no cacheComponents flag exists, unstable_cache is the right choice, with the cache key built from the serialized args. I'm considering whether to include workspaceId in the key too, since identical findings content across tenants would otherwise produce the same cached wording—harmless, but safer to scope it per workspace anyway. I also need to think through how rephrase failures, like a missing API key, should propagate when thrown inside the cached function.

If the function throws, the result won't be cached, so errors should throw rather than return null, which I'll catch outside the cache boundary — that avoids accidentally caching a null fallback. I also want to tighten the deterministic fallback sentence, using the title plus the first sentence of the detail instead of the verbose default.

For validation, I'm setting up a rule where every number in the AI output must appear in the input title/detail using a digit-token regex, which means computed facts like a derived percentage would fail and fall back to the deterministic sentence — I'm keeping this strict rather than injecting extra computed numbers to allow nicer phrasing. I also checked that reformatted dates like "12 Oct" versus "2026-10-12" still pass since the regex splits on non-digit characters, extracting matching tokens either way. Now I'm drafting the actual prompt instructing the AI to rewrite each finding as one or two short plain sentences for a weekly money summary.

For the UI, I'm working out header details: evidence chip labels formatted as "E{n} · label," a header reading "✦ Weekly briefing" with a subtitle noting the count of verified findings, and sorting out what "Mute type" should link to since it's ambiguous at the row level — I've decided to make it a header-level "Customize" link to the settings page's mute-types section, alongside a "Dismiss all" action tied to the dismissInsight logic.

content.thinking:
I'm tracing through where each test navigates after adding an account — goal-reservations goes back to "/" to use Update balance, while the accounts page flow redirects to /money/accounts, so I need to adjust each test's navigation and form-filling steps accordingly.

Now I'm worried about whether "Add account" is clickable as a button role, since it's actually a `<summary>` element toggling a disclosure — Playwright's role computation for summary is uncertain across browsers, so clicking by role name might be unreliable. I'm considering scoping the locator to the specific form containing the "Name" field to avoid ambiguity with other forms on the accounts page that might also have a name input (like a rename form).

I'll scope by finding the `details` element whose `summary` text matches "Add account", then use that scoped locator for the name field and submit button, which should be reliable since the label-input association looks standard. I also need to make sure other flows navigate to the accounts page first, since headings they check for visibility depend on being on that page.

The Accounts page uses its own "Add account" popover with Name/Currency fields and redirects to `/money/accounts`, so I'll repoint the four flows there, keeping `goal-reservations` returning to Home for the Update balance step.

I'll also drop the "Import statement" button from the header, keep Edit layout, and skip adding a month toggle pill since only month view is needed.

For defaults, I'm updating the widget key order to include overview, insights, upcoming, spending, budgets, accounts, and agents, and making sure dashboardItems(null) returns this new default set. The tricky part is existing users who already saved a custom layout — since pinning an artifact triggers a save, they'd be stuck with the old widget set and wouldn't automatically see budgets or agents. I'm weighing whether to migrate old saved layouts or just let users reset manually via Edit layout, since cleanly detecting "newly added" vs "intentionally removed" keys isn't straightforward.

I'll switch the grid to 6 columns so Accounts and Agent team can sit side by side at half width, and place the agent-team banner as an `agents` widget in that slot for now, with tile-grid restyling to follow in a second pass.

The output works, but the wording feels clunky since it leans on source phrasing like "including supported rollover" and raw dates. I want to loosen the prompt so the model can write month names like "October" instead of "2026-10," and phrase things more like a friendly briefing that leads with what matters most.

The tricky part is computed figures—something like "€6.00 over" requires a derived number that isn't directly in the facts. I could bake those derived amounts into the deterministic detail text itself in insights.ts (e.g. "€156.00 spent against €150.00 allowance — €6.00 over"), but that risks breaking existing test assertions on detail text, so I want to keep that change minimal or avoid it. Instead I'll focus on prompt wording: tell it to write one short, friendly sentence leading with what matters, copy amounts exactly, spell out months/dates in words, and drop methodology caveats unless relevant.

I also need to revert the debug logs I added, and since the wording is cached via unstable_cache keyed on findings, I should bump the cache key version (e.g. add "v2") so the prompt change actually takes effect instead of serving stale cached text.

The AI path works and passes fact checks, but the output is bland since it copies the code's wording verbatim. I'll tighten the prompt to match the mockup's style (spelled-out months, leading with key info, no caveats), strip the debug logs, and bump the cache key version so stale wording isn't reused.

content.text:
The new Overview is built on the branch `t3/overview-redesign`, in 12 commits. Nothing is pushed yet. With demo data loaded it matches the mockup's layout: net worth with month card, then briefing with Coming up, cash flow with Budgets, and Accounts with Agent team.

**What changed on Home**
- **Net worth:** a 12-month line chart and "+€X this month · +Y%". It reuses the same month-end figures as the Wealth page. The "by currency" dropdown is gone, and per your answer only the display currency counts. The other-currency work is listed in `BACKLOG.md`.
- **October cash flow (right side):** In, Out, a split bar, "Left this month", and the forecaster's lowest point.
- **Cash flow · 6 months:** In and Out bars side by side. Clicking **In** shows only income and lists where the money came from. Clicking **Out** shows only spending, with that month's top categories and merchants. Clicking a bar picks the month. Clicking In or Out on the month card jumps there too.
- **Coming up:** date tiles, the account under each payment, and the total for the next 30 days.
- **Budgets:** a new card showing spent of limit, with "€X left for N days", "€X over" in orange, rolled-over amounts, or "On track". It uses the same budget maths as the insights.
- **Weekly briefing:** this replaces Important insights. It only shows big things: forecast shortfalls, budgets at 80% or more, unusual charges, big spending jumps, and changed recurring payments. With none of those, the card doesn't appear.
  - The wording is rewritten by the AI model set for the agent team.
  - If the AI's sentence adds or changes any number, the app shows its own text instead, so amounts always come from your data.
  - The wording is saved per finding, so the AI only runs again when the facts change.
  - It has Dismiss, Dismiss all, and Mute type.
- **Accounts:** compact rows with a letter icon, a BANK or MANUAL label, "synced 2 hours ago", and **Import file** / **Connect bank** buttons. Adding an account is now only on the Accounts page. I kept a small **Update balance** link on each row, because that form can confirm a balance without retyping it and the Accounts page form can't.
- **Layout:** Recent transactions, Available funds and Goals are off by default but can be switched back on in Edit layout, along with pinned artifacts. The Import button is gone from the header, and the date line no longer ends in "· EUR".

**Things to know**
- **Saved layouts:** if your own workspace already has a saved layout (pinning an artifact saves one), you won't see Budgets or Agent team until you tick them in Edit layout. New layouts get the new design.
- **AI wording needs a model it can reach:** your `.env` only has an OpenRouter key, but the default Agent team model is an OpenAI one. Until you set an OpenRouter model (e.g. `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`) for the Agent team in Settings, the briefing shows the app's own text. I tested the AI path that way on the QA account, then switched it back.
- **Subagents:** I didn't use any. Almost every step edited the same page file, so parallel agents would have collided and cost more.

**Tests**
- Lint and build pass.
- `npm test` has 14 failures, all in the import and agent tests that already fail on `main` without `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- In the end-to-end tests, 7 of the 9 flows I touched pass. Two (`dated-overview`, `two-user-isolation`) still fail outside Home: one on a balance check before the browser opens, one on `/api/imports/:id` returning a 500. They had been crashing in their own cleanup, which hid the real errors, and I fixed that cleanup.
- The QA workspace has been reset.

**Not done yet (the second pass)**
- The Agent team card is still the old banner, moved into its new slot; the 7-tile grid with "Review N proposals" comes next.
- The History strip with Undo.
- The "Preview move" button on shortfalls and "Price up €2.00" on Coming up.

Should I open a PR for this, or start on Agent team and History first?

Now I'm sketching a small loader module that queries recurring series with their assumption ids, then pulls the linked transaction amounts, currency, and posted dates through the embedded relationship, working out how Supabase's query syntax handles the nested transaction fields.

I'm deciding to split this into two separate queries instead—fetching link rows first, then transactions by id in chunks of 100—to avoid any precision or embedding issues with casting the amount column, then I'll join in the assumption names to build a map keyed by account and name pointing to the price change amount. Finally I'll use that to show a subtitle line like "Price up €2.00" styled in warning or brand color depending on direction.

I'll detect a price change only when a confirmed recurring payment's two latest recorded transactions differ in amount, matching the change to the upcoming payment via its assumption. Starting with the pure function and its test.

content.text:
The four remaining pieces are done, and the app is running for you at **http://localhost:3100**.

To see it with demo data, sign in as the QA user. The email and password are in `.env` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL` / `E2E_USER_PASSWORD`. I've loaded six months of data that exercises every card. If you sign in with your own account instead, any layout you saved earlier won't show the new cards (Budgets, Agent team, History) until you switch them on in **Edit layout**.

What I added:
- **Agent team:** seven tiles showing each agent's result from the last run, with "last run 14:55 · 4m 12s" in the header. One button underneath: **Review N proposals**, or **Watch live** while a run is going, or **Run agent team** when there's nothing to review.
- **History:** the four newest changes, from imports, balances you set, wealth edits, and agent proposals you approved. **Undo** opens the page where that change is undone, so the existing safety checks and previews there still apply. It doesn't undo in one click from Home.
- **Price up / Price down** on Coming up: shown when a confirmed recurring payment's last two real charges differ (e.g. Spotify "Price up EUR 2.00").
- **Shortfall and Preview move** in the weekly briefing:
  - It flags an account the forecast takes below its protected amount, even when your total is fine.
  - It names the account with the most to spare, for example: "N26 Main is set to run short around 1 Nov… moving EUR 419.88 from Holiday reserve would cover it."
  - **Preview move** opens Plan's existing funding preview. I clicked it in the demo: N26 Main ends at EUR 0.00 instead of going short, your total stays the same, and nothing is saved.
  - My first version saved a what-if scenario instead. That made the move look like it cost EUR 83.98, because the scenario tool counts each half of a transfer separately, so I switched to the funding preview.

Checks:
- `npm test`: the same 14 failures as on `main`, all in tests that need `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- Lint is clean and the build compiles.
- I didn't rerun the end-to-end tests after these four additions. The earlier run's results still stand: two tests outside Home fail.

**Two things in your setup:**
- **AI wording in the briefing:** the briefing only gets AI wording when the Agent team model is an OpenRouter one, since `.env` only has an OpenRouter key. The QA account is set to `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` so you can see it. Your own account still has the default OpenAI model, so it would show the app's plain wording.
- **Port 3000:** that port is serving a different, older copy of the app, so don't judge the new design there.

Everything is in 19 commits on `t3/overview-redesign`, not pushed. Tell me what you'd change once you've looked. When you're happy I can open a PR and reset the QA account.

content.thinking:
I'm spotting a real bug: the net worth chart shows flat zero before October 2026 because the balance series only pulls from balance_snapshots, and the synced bank account only has one snapshot taken at sync time, even though transaction history goes back further. I could reconstruct historical balances by working backward from the latest snapshot, subtracting posted transactions after each target date — that would be deterministic and accurate.

But going earlier than the first known transaction, we have no basis for a number, so the chart should stop rather than drop to zero, and the "+EUR 27.11 this month" delta is misleading since it's comparing against an unknown prior balance. I also want to check how far back the bank sync actually fetches transactions, since PSD2 providers like GoCardless or Enable Banking usually cap history at 90 days to two years.

Separately, the briefing paraphrasing issue traces back to the account defaulting to OpenAI with no API key configured, falling back to a plain-text formatter whose wording is clunky — I'm thinking about improving that fallback phrasing, like cleaning up date ranges and dropping awkward year-month strings.

I'll convert raw ISO date strings into friendlier human phrasing deterministically, so things like date ranges become "1–26 Oct" style snippets, and single dates or month tokens get similarly simplified, giving the title sentence a cleaner flow like comparing groceries spending across two periods directly. content.text:
I've fixed both problems and made both changes. They're live at http://localhost:3100; refresh to see them.

**1. Net worth before you connected the bank:** Moneo did fetch your earlier transactions; the sync asks the bank for its full history. For your Revolut account the bank gave 138 transactions back to 21 July. The problem was that the chart only used recorded balances, and the first one is from 15 October, when you connected.
- Earlier month ends are now worked out from that first balance by taking off every posted transaction since.
- I only go back to the day before your first transaction. Before 21 July nothing is on record, so the line now starts at the end of July instead of drawing a fake €0.
- "This month" is only shown when there's a balance for the end of last month to compare against. That removes the wrong "+EUR 27.11".

**2. The briefing wasn't being rewritten by AI.** Your Agent team model is still the default OpenAI one, and this machine only has an OpenRouter key, so the AI call fails and you see the app's own text.
- That text is now readable without AI: "Groceries spending increased: EUR 327.30 in 1–26 Oct, compared with EUR 30.71 in 5–30 Sept."
- To get the AI wording, set **Settings → AI models → Agent team** to an OpenRouter model such as `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`. That's what I tested with, and it produced sentences like "Groceries are over budget: EUR 547.50 spent of EUR 450.00 this month." I can set it on your account if you'd like.

**3. Net worth hover:** moving the mouse over the line now shows a dashed guide, a dot, and a small card with the exact amount and date (e.g. "EUR 14720.00 · 31 May 2026").

**4. Cash flow · 6 months:**
- The buttons at the top are now **Both · In · Out**, and they're the only thing that hides bars. **Both** always brings both back.
- Clicking a bar opens that month's breakdown (where money came from, or top categories and merchants). Both series stay visible and the other months fade, so you can see which month you're looking at.

Unit tests show the same 14 known failures that need `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Lint is clean, the build compiles, and I checked the hover and the cash-flow behaviour in the browser on the QA account. Everything is committed on `t3/overview-redesign` (now 27 commits, not pushed).
